text: Duck Plague is a viral disease of ducks and other waterfowl, following a very acute course with rapid spread and sudden deaths. Symptoms: strong light sensitivity — sick ducks seek dark areas with closed eyes; ataxia (loss of coordination); extreme thirst; severe diarrhea; occasionally a prolapsed penis; tremor and partial paralysis. Necropsy findings: severe enteritis; crusty plaques from the esophagus to the bursa (yellowish in later stages); hemorrhage in the intestine, body cavities, and heart. Treatment: none, since it's viral, though — unusually — vaccine can be used both to stop further spread and, atypically, to treat already-infected birds.
